sources.title: Anne Thomas, The Banach-Tarski Paradox and Amenability, Lecture 20: Invariant Mean implies Reiter's Property (University of Sydney Honours lecture notes)
sources.locator: Complete 18-page lecture (slides 1-18, file pp. 1-18): UCB(G), convolution smoothing, topological invariant means, the Mazur closure step and the derivation of Reiter's property from an invariant mean.

contents.name: The space UCB(G) of left-uniformly continuous bounded functions and its basic properties (nonempty, invariant, translation-continuous)
If f is in L^1(G)_{1,+} and phi in L-infinity(G) then f*phi is in UCB(G), with the approximate-identity computation m(f*phi)=m(phi)
Definition of the topological invariant mean m-tilde(phi)=m(f_0*phi) and its invariance

Conclusion: norm-approximately invariant densities and the Reiter property
Almost invariant L^2 vectors as the regular-representation translation of Reiter's property

sources.title: Matthew Daws and Volker Runde, Reiter's properties (P1) and (P2) for locally compact quantum groups, arXiv:0705.3432v5
sources.locator: Introduction, p. 1 (invariant means and weak-star cluster points) and Section 1, pp. 2-4 (Reiter's property (P_p) for p in [1,infinity), the case p=1, and weak-star density of normal states).

contents.name: Introduction, p. 1, equation (1) and the paragraph after it: a locally compact group is amenable iff there is an invariant mean on L-infinity(G), and every weak* accumulation point of the mean-valued net is left invariant
Section 1, p. 2: the display defining Reiter's property (P_p) and the case p=1, matching the compact-uniform net formulation
Section 1, p. 4: weak*-density of normal states in the state space, used as the abstract model for the density of probability densities in the mean set
The quantum-group (P2) material and local compact quantum groups of Sections 2-5
contents.reason: This pair concerns locally compact groups only; no item consumes quantum groups, multipliers or the (P2) property.
